verdict.rationale: Codex documents its own event-surface entry points: cloud tasks can be started from GitHub PRs, GitLab merge requests and issues, Linear issues and Slack threads. It also offers `codex exec` for non-interactive runs in CI pipelines, and delegated cloud tasks run in parallel. However, the evidence shows these starts as user-initiated, and any scheduling would come from the user's CI rather than Codex. missing for 10: native recurring schedules, always-on or event-automatic agents that run without a human starting them, autonomous maintain-and-fix loops, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to maintain and fix my software autonomously

citations.quote: Start work in Codex cloud from GitHub pull requests, GitLab merge requests and issues, Linear issues, or Slack channels and threads.
Use Codex interactively or call codex exec from repeatable workflows and pipelines.
Delegate a longer task and return when it is ready.
